problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=8y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-8x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(-1) \\ y(-1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(8t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}].$*

| $[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c,
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t+1)}\,x(-1) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8(t+1)) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(8(t+1)) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(8(t+1)) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(8(t+1))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡(8(t+1))\, \\ \,5\operatorname{cos}⁡(8(t+1))\,\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
